title: Morphism sheafification of a fibred groupoid
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-topos] whose objects and arrows form sets in the larger universe; all groupoids and their morphism sets below belong to that universe. A fibred groupoid has cartesian pullbacks along every base arrow, with their coherent comparison isomorphisms. A prestack is a fibred groupoid whose presheaves of isomorphisms on slice sites are sheaves. A stack is a prestack in which covering descent data for objects are effective. Let $\mathcal P$ be a fibred groupoid. Keep its fibre objects and replace, for $u,v\in\mathcal P(T)$, its presheaf $I_{u,v}$ of isomorphisms on $\mathcal C/T$ by its set-valued sheafification $I_{u,v}^{\#}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Take the new arrows $u\to v$ in the fibre over $T$ to be $I_{u,v}^{\#}(1_T)$. Composition, identities, inverses, and pullback extend those of $\mathcal P$, and give a fibred groupoid $\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pre}}$ with these objects and arrows. It is a prestack, and the sheafification maps define an objectwise identity pullback-compatible functor $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pre}}$. Its isomorphism sheaf between $q(u),q(v)$ is canonically $I_{u,v}^{\#}$, compatibly with the map from $I_{u,v}$. For any prestack $\mathcal Z$ and pullback-compatible functor $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Z$, there is a pullback-compatible functor $F^{\mathrm{pre}}:\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pre}}\to\mathcal Z$ and an invertible natural transformation $F^{\mathrm{pre}}q\cong F$.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, quotient locally equal arrows and add locally defined arrows, first four construction paragraphs; Tag 0435 (lemma-stackify-universal-property), extension on morphisms into a prestack.

proof.text: Work on covering sieves throughout; no fibre products in $\mathcal C$ are assumed. Use [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] for slice restriction and relocalization. For $u,v\in\mathcal P(T)$ put $A_{u,v}=I_{u,v}^{\#}$, using [lem-trf-sieve-set-sheafification-exists] on $\mathcal C/T$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] shows that sheafifying its unit $\eta:I_{u,v}\to A_{u,v}$ gives an isomorphism: the sheafification of a sheaf is itself, and both composites are identities by uniqueness of factorization. Hence [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] makes $\eta$ locally surjective and locally injective. Thus sections of $A_{u,v}$ have local representatives in $I_{u,v}$; representatives of the same section become equal on a covering sieve. Intersections of finitely many covering sieves cover: for two, pull back the second along every arrow of the first and apply transitivity [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Iterating gives simultaneous representatives of any finite list of sections.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: Construct composition on $\mathcal C/T$ explicitly. For $a\in A_{u,v}(f)$ and $b\in A_{v,w}(f)$ choose a common covering sieve of $\operatorname{dom}(f)$ representing them by arrows $a_r,b_r$ of $\mathcal P$. On each member take $\eta(b_r\circ a_r)$. For any two choices, their restrictions to any common further arrow have equal images for $a$ and $b$; local injectivity from [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] makes both pairs of representatives equal after a common covering refinement. Their composites then agree there, and separatedness of $A_{u,w}$ makes their images equal before that refinement. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-topos] therefore glues these sections uniquely to $b\circ a$. The same argument proves independence of the covering and representatives. Restricting the chosen sieve and its representatives gives the construction after any base arrow, so composition is a morphism of presheaves. Set $1_u=\eta(1_u)$ and define $a^{-1}$ by gluing $\eta(a_r^{-1})$; local equality of representatives and separatedness prove that this too is independent of choices and commutes with restriction.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: For three composable sections choose simultaneous representatives, as in step 1. On this covering sieve the two bracketings of their composite are the images of $(c_r\circ b_r)\circ a_r=c_r\circ(b_r\circ a_r)$ in $\mathcal P$. Separatedness [def-weil-pbc-topos] gives global associativity. The equations $a\circ1=a=1\circ a$, $a^{-1}\circ a=1$ and $a\circ a^{-1}=1$ follow in exactly the same explicit way: represent $a$ locally, use the corresponding identity in its original fibre groupoid, and use separatedness. Consequently each fibre with objects those of $\mathcal P(T)$ and arrows $A_{u,v}(1_T)$ is a groupoid. Also $\eta(b\circ a)=\eta(b)\circ\eta(a)$ and $\eta(1)=1$ by the construction on original representatives; thus $q_T$ is a functor, identity on objects.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: Let $h:S\to T$. Relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies $(\mathcal C/T)/(S\to T)$ with $\mathcal C/S$. The original pullback comparisons identify the restriction of $I_{u,v}$ with $I_{h^*u,h^*v}$ by conjugation. Apply [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] on $\mathcal C/T$ at $(S,h)$ to obtain a unit-compatible isomorphism $A_{u,v}|_{\mathcal C/S}\cong A_{h^*u,h^*v}$. Define $h^*$ on new arrows by restriction followed by this isomorphism. It preserves composition, identity and inversion: on local representatives these assertions are respectively the corresponding assertions for the original pullback functor, and separatedness makes them hold for all sections. Take the identity and composition comparisons for these pullbacks to be the images under $q$ of the original comparisons. Their naturality on new arrows follows by the same local-representative check. Their unit equations and associativity (cocycle) equation $c_{h,\ell k}\circ h^*(c_{k,\ell})=c_{kh,\ell}\circ c_{h,k}$ (on $\ell^*$ applied to an object) already hold on each object in $\mathcal P$, so their images under the fibre functors $q_T$ satisfy those equations. This gives coherent pullbacks; the unit compatibility also makes $q$ pullback-compatible.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: For completeness, assemble the total fibred category directly. Its objects are pairs $(T,u)$ with $u\in\mathcal P(T)$. An arrow $(S,u)\to(T,v)$ is $(h,a)$ with $h:S\to T$ and $a:u\to h^*v$ a new fibre arrow. Write $c_{h,k}:h^*k^*\cong(kh)^*$ for the comparisons from step 4. Define $(k,b)\circ(h,a)=(kh,c_{h,k}\circ h^*(b)\circ a)$; identities use the inverse of the pullback identity comparison. Substitution in this formula shows that associativity is the associativity (cocycle) equation for $c$, its naturality, and fibre associativity; the unit equations give the two identity laws. The arrow $(h,1):(S,h^*v)\to(T,v)$ is cartesian: any arrow $(h\ell,b)$ factors over $\ell$ uniquely through it by the vertical component $c_{\ell,h}^{-1}\circ b$. These formulas prove the factorization and uniqueness. All vertical arrows are invertible by step 3, so the result is a category fibred in groupoids. An original arrow over $h$ factors uniquely through the chosen original cartesian lift, and sending its vertical factor by $q_S$ defines the asserted functor on total categories. The composition formula and step 4 show that it preserves composition and the cartesian lifts. No objects are added.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: For $h:S\to T$, the arrows between $h^*q(u)$ and $h^*q(v)$ in the new fibre are $A_{h^*u,h^*v}(1_S)$. The unit-compatible isomorphism of step 4 identifies this set with $A_{u,v}(h)$. Its naturality identifies restriction maps as well. Thus the entire isomorphism presheaf between $q(u)$ and $q(v)$ is canonically $A_{u,v}=I_{u,v}^{\#}$, not merely its value at $1_T$; its map from $I_{u,v}$ is $\eta$ by the unit equation in [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification]. Each such presheaf is a sheaf, so the new fibred groupoid is a prestack by the definition in the item.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, first four construction paragraphs; the omitted checks are supplied explicitly for groupoids.

proof.text: Let $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Z$ be as in the statement, and write $K_{u,v}=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Z}(F(u),F(v))$ on $\mathcal C/T$. This is a sheaf because $\mathcal Z$ is a prestack. The original $F$, together with its pullback comparisons, gives a presheaf map $I_{u,v}\to K_{u,v}$. By [lem-trf-sieve-set-sheafification-exists], it extends uniquely to a sheaf map $\phi_{u,v}:A_{u,v}\to K_{u,v}$. Define $F_T^{\mathrm{pre}}(u)=F_T(u)$ and its map on arrows by $\phi_{u,v}(1_T)$. On a simultaneous local representation of two new arrows, $\phi$ sends their composite to $F(b_r\circ a_r)=F(b_r)\circ F(a_r)$; separatedness of $K_{u,w}$ gives preservation of composition globally. Identities are preserved since $\phi\eta=F$ on original arrows, and preservation of inverses follows from the inverse equations. Hence these are functors on fibres.

source.place: Tag 0435 (lemma-stackify-universal-property), morphism-gluing part of the hint; restricted to the morphism stage of Tag 02ZN; effectivity of objects is not used.

proof.text: Use the original pullback comparisons of $F$ as the pullback comparisons of $F^{\mathrm{pre}}$, with the same object components. Their naturality for a new arrow is checked on local representatives by [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection]: unit compatibility of [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] identifies its pullback with the image of the original pulled-back arrow; the required square is then the original naturality square of $F$. Separatedness of the target isomorphism sheaf gives the square globally. The unit and composition coherence equations involve the unchanged object components and follow from those of $F$. The total-category formula of step 5 now gives a pullback-compatible functor $F^{\mathrm{pre}}$. The equality $\phi\eta=F$ identifies $F^{\mathrm{pre}}q$ with $F$ on every fibre and on the chosen cartesian lifts, hence on all arrows. Identity object components give the claimed invertible natural transformation. None of this uses effectivity of object descent in $\mathcal Z$.
